answer.origin: Third-party media view: Keithen Drury, The Motley Fool article published 2026-07-06 (https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/07/06/nvidia-stock-is-below-200-per-share-again-heres/). The article relays an average analyst FY2028 (ending January 2028) EPS forecast of $12.76 without naming the analysts, count, or estimate date. It also relays management's hyperscaler spending outlook from Nvidia's last quarterly call, which the article does not date precisely.
answer.note: The article supports a conditional read that Wall Street consensus for Nvidia's fiscal 2028 EPS is about $12.76, and that analysts expect 82% revenue growth for the rest of calendar 2026 and 41% for 2027. Those figures are secondhand and lack stated definitions, so they show what the article's author reports rather than a verified consensus. The article attributes to management a forecast that hyperscaler spending will top $1 trillion in 2027 after about $650 billion in 2026. That is a customer-capex demand signal relayed secondhand, not Nvidia's order or revenue figure. The author's $319 implied price (EPS of $12.76 times a 25 multiple) and his view that the stock could reach $300 in late 2027 are his own valuation opinions, not source facts, and they rest on the unverified consensus. The author's view that the consensus is conservative is an opinion and carries no independent evidential weight.
limitations: The $12.76 FY2028 EPS consensus is not tied to an identified analyst set, count, provider, or estimate date, and the article does not say whether it is GAAP or non-GAAP.
The 82% (rest of 2026) and 41% (2027) growth figures have no stated base period, revenue or EPS definition, or consensus provider.

The management hyperscaler spending figures ($650B in 2026 and over $1T in 2027) are relayed from an unidentified 'last quarterly conference call' with no call date or transcript in the record, and the hyperscaler scope and definition are not stated.
The article gives no Nvidia filing, transcript, or primary source for any of these figures; the author's own valuation inputs (multiple of 25) are not sourced.
follow_up: Identify the consensus provider and the estimate date, count, and EPS basis (GAAP or non-GAAP) for the FY2028 $12.76 figure.
Check Nvidia's most recent earnings call transcript to confirm the $650B (2026) and $1T-plus (2027) hyperscaler spending statements, their exact wording, and the hyperscaler definition used.
Verify the 82% and 41% growth rates against consensus revenue estimates for the matching periods and definitions before using them as a consensus figure.
Check whether any of the relayed consensus figures have been revised in later provider data or in Nvidia's subsequent quarterly reports.
